questions.enonce_markdown:
One of the phases of SDLC is Feasibility Studies.

(a) List all the phases of SDLC in logical order. (2 marks)

(b) Explain two activities carried out by the system analyst at the feasibility phase. (2 marks)

(c) State and describe two conversion methods use to implement a new system in an organization. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Phases of the SDLC (systems development life cycle) in logical order (2 marks).**

1. Problem definition (preliminary investigation)
2. Feasibility study
3. Systems analysis (requirements gathering)
4. System design
5. Development (programming or coding)
6. Testing
7. Implementation (installation and changeover)
8. Maintenance and review (evaluation)

(Some textbooks start the list with the feasibility study or group some phases together; the same logical order is kept.)

**(b) Two activities of the system analyst at the feasibility phase (2 marks)** (any two, each explained):

- **Studying the problem and the present system** to understand what the organisation needs and what the new system must do.
- **Assessing whether the proposed solution is feasible:** technically (is the hardware and software available?), economically (a cost-benefit analysis: do the benefits exceed the costs?), operationally (will the users accept and be able to use it?) and in time (can it be finished by the deadline?).
- **Proposing alternative solutions** and **writing a feasibility report** with a recommendation for management, who decide whether the project goes ahead.

**(c) Two conversion (changeover) methods (2 marks)** (any two, each stated and described):

- **Direct changeover:** the old system is **stopped on a fixed date and the new system is started at once**. It is cheap and fast, but risky: if the new system fails there is nothing to fall back on.
- **Parallel running:** the **old and the new systems are run together for a period** and their results are compared, then the old system is dropped. It is very safe but expensive, because the work is done twice.
- **Phased (gradual) changeover:** the new system is introduced **part by part** (one module at a time). *Pilot changeover:* the new system is first used in **one branch or department** before the others.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Project managing activities are the sole responsibility of the project manager.

(a) List four activities carryout by the project manager. (2 marks)

(b) Describe two ways that project managers control projects. (2 marks)

(c) Explain why is it important to identify the critical path of a project? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Four activities carried out by the project manager (2 marks)** (any four):

- **Planning** the project: defining its objectives, scope and the tasks to be done.
- **Scheduling** the tasks and setting milestones and deadlines.
- **Organising and allocating resources** (people, equipment and money) to the tasks.
- **Preparing and controlling the budget** (costs).
- **Monitoring the progress** of the work and reporting to management.
- **Managing risks and problems**, and leading and communicating with the team and the client.

**(b) Two ways of controlling a project (2 marks)** (any two, each described):

- **Monitoring progress against the plan** with tools such as a Gantt chart, PERT or critical path charts and regular progress meetings and reports, so that delays are seen early and corrective action is taken.
- **Controlling cost and quality:** comparing the money spent with the budget, and checking the work done (tests, reviews) against the requirements.
- **Managing risks and changes:** identifying possible problems in advance, and approving any change to the scope only after its effect on time and cost has been studied.

**(c) Importance of the critical path (1 mark).** The critical path is the **longest chain of dependent tasks, and it fixes the shortest possible time in which the project can be finished**. A delay in **any task on the critical path delays the whole project**, so the manager knows which tasks must be watched closely and given priority and resources, while other tasks have some slack (float).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carry out the following conversions.

(a) $56.12_{10}$ to binary. (2 marks)

(b) $10111101_{2}$ to octal. (2 marks)

(c) $B73E_{16}$ to binary. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) $56.12_{10}$ to binary (2 marks).**

*Integer part:* repeated division by 2 gives $56 = 111000_2$ (56 = 32 + 16 + 8).

*Fractional part:* repeated multiplication of the fraction by 2, keeping the integer part each time:

| Fraction | x 2 | Integer part |
|---|---|---|
| 0.12 | 0.24 | 0 |
| 0.24 | 0.48 | 0 |
| 0.48 | 0.96 | 0 |
| 0.96 | 1.92 | 1 |
| 0.92 | 1.84 | 1 |
| 0.84 | 1.68 | 1 |
| 0.68 | 1.36 | 1 |
| 0.36 | 0.72 | 0 |
| 0.72 | 1.44 | 1 |

Reading the integer parts downwards: $0.12_{10} = 0.000111101\ldots_2$ (the fraction never ends exactly).

$$56.12_{10} = 111000.000111101\ldots_2 \approx 111000.0001111_2$$

(The 8-place value $111000.00011110_2$ is $56.1171875$, which is close to 56.12.)

**(b) $10111101_2$ to octal (2 marks).** Group the bits in threes starting from the right (add a leading zero): $010\ 111\ 101$. Each group is one octal digit: $010 = 2$, $111 = 7$, $101 = 5$.

$$10111101_2 = 275_8$$

Check: $10111101_2 = 189$ and $2 \times 64 + 7 \times 8 + 5 = 189$.

**(c) $B73E_{16}$ to binary (2 marks).** Replace each hexadecimal digit by its 4-bit group: $B = 1011$, $7 = 0111$, $3 = 0011$, $E = 1110$.

$$B73E_{16} = 1011\ 0111\ 0011\ 1110_2$$

Check: both forms equal $46910_{10}$.
